manifest.name: dsh-win-multi-bash
manifest.author: Dinosaur_MC
manifest.description: Windows multi-bash plugin for dsh: git_bash, wsl_bash and opt-in msys2_bash model tools, an opt-in ssh row that serves ssh_shell (commands over a pooled ssh2 connection: a host registry, per-call exec channels) and ssh_scp (SFTP file and tree transfers on the same pooled connection), and a terminal tool that keeps a persistent PTY session — its ssh sessions still use the OpenSSH client. Each dialect owns its own executor and leaves the ctx.shell seat to dsh's own pwsh executor.

bundle.text:
# dsh-win-multi-bash — self-contained Windows multi-bash wiring.
#
# This patch is the whole plugin: it inserts the plugin's own rows. Every
# inserted row loads code from THIS package through its BARE package name (the core
# row, which serves ./client and ./factory), through ./tool-git-bash,
# ./tool-wsl-bash, ./tool-msys2-bash and ./tool-ssh-shell, or through
# ./tool-terminal — nothing depends on runtime packages beyond the published
# @deepseek-ai base packages (dsh-bash-local, dsh-sandbox, dsh-tools, dsh-shell,
# dsh-llm, ...). `ssh_shell` and `ssh_scp` additionally use the `ssh2` package for
# their transport: exec channels and SFTP transfers on one pooled connection per host,
# with host-key verification on every dial (see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES).
#
# ── What the rows do ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#   win-mb-plugin       — the package row: the plugin's core row. `name` is the
#                         BARE package specifier and the module is the package
#                         main, which does two things.
#                         (1) It carries the browser half. The Web client
#                             discovers one by resolving a row's package name to
#                             its package.json (dsh-client-modules:
#                             locatePkgJson → exactPackageSpecifier, which
#                             answers `undefined` for a subpath) and reading
#                             `dsh.client` + the `./client` export there. The
#                             tool rows are subpaths, so without this row
#                             `lib/client.js` is never served and the tool rows
#                             show no Configure page on the Plugins page.
#                         (2) It owns the ONE prompt section the four family
#                             tools share (`tool:win-mb-bash`, order = midpoint
#                             of dsh's TOOL_BASH/TOOL_PWSH). Its text is resolved
#                             per assembly from the tools actually mounted, so it
#                             says nothing when no family tool is enabled and
#                             never assumes another tool — or pwsh — is present.
#                             Shared guidance lives here once instead of once per
#                             tool description; each tool description keeps only
#                             its own dialect facts.
#                         This is the one row that must not be switched off:
#                         there is no supported way to mark a third-party row
#                         read-only (dsh's plugin manager locks only rows from
#                         its own protected-module list, its own row, and rows
#                         it cannot address), so instead the composition is
#                         built so that nothing can half-break: switch it off
#                         and the tools keep working — their descriptions fall
#                         back to carrying the shared guidance themselves — and
#                         only the Plugins-page configuration disappears.
#   win-mb-tool-git     — registers the model-facing `git_bash` tool
#                         (MSYS dialect) into the host tools registry: every
#                         session sees it regardless of its agent preset. The
#                         tool owns its own GitBashExecutor; its model-facing
#                         description carries only the MSYS facts and reminds
#                         the model that MSYS paths are valid only inside Git
#                         Bash — dsh's file tools on Windows take native
#                         C:\... paths.
#   win-mb-tool-wsl     — the `wsl_bash` tool, owning its own WslBashExecutor;
#                         its description carries only the WSL facts.
#                         **Opt-in**: the row ships disabled (`disabled: true`)
#                         because a WSL deployment is a second toolchain many
#                         Windows machines do not have, and probing it at boot
#                         costs the row's first load. Enable it in the Plugins
#                         panel to add the tool.
#   win-mb-tool-msys2   — the `msys2_bash` tool, owning its own Msys2BashExecutor.
#                         **Opt-in**: the row ships disabled (`disabled: true`)
#                         and the user enables it. It exists to prove the
#                         skeleton: adding a shell is one executor file plus one
#                         declaration in lib/shell-dialects.js.
#   win-mb-tool-ssh     — the `ssh_shell` and `ssh_scp` tools, sharing ONE
#                         SshShellExecutor (and so one host registry, one policy, one
#                         pooled connection per host): the family's only REMOTE
#                         dialect (`effects: 'remote'` in the registry). `ssh_shell`
#                         runs commands over per-call exec channels; `ssh_scp` moves
#                         files and trees over SFTP on that same connection.
#                         **Opt-in** for the same reason plus one of its own — it
#                         needs a host, which only a deployment can name. Nothing
#                         local bounds its file effects, so it reports
#                         `sandbox: { mode, remote: true }` rather than a verdict.
#
# Every inserted row is win32-only; POSIX keeps the base bundle's own bash wiring.
# The tool rows are independent of each other and of the core row — the section
# follows whichever subset is mounted, and the core row's absence degrades to
# the fallback described above rather than to a broken prompt.
#
# ── Why nothing here touches the ctx.shell seat ──────────────────────────────
# dsh 0.1.7 removed the shell seam's routing field (`ShellExecRequest.shell`),
# which is what the pre-0.1.7 design used: one selector executor occupying
# `ctx.shell` and dispatching each request to a backend by name. With no
# routing input there is nothing for a selector to select on — the tool is
# what knows which shell it wants — so each of our tools now owns exactly one
# executor and drives it directly, and `ctx.shell` is left entirely to the
# base bundle's own row (`pwsh-sandbox` on win32, `bash-sandbox` elsewhere).
#
# That is also why this patch no longer disables `pwsh-sandbox`: the base
# bundle's pwsh executor is what keeps `ctx.shell` (and therefore dsh's own
# `tool-pwsh` and `permission-presets`, which inject `shell`) alive. pwsh
# remains the default shell for the composition; it is simply served by dsh
# itself rather than by us.

- insert:
    # The core row. Bare specifier on purpose: this is the row that lets the Web
    # client find this package's `dsh.client` declaration, and the row that owns
    # the shared prompt section (see the header note). Keep it enabled — with it
    # off the tools still run and still carry the shared guidance themselves, but
    # the Plugins page loses its Configure pages.
    - id: win-mb-plugin
      name: 'dsh-win-multi-bash'
      disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'
      # The deployment-wide sandbox private-temp self-heal, declared ONCE here
      # (default ON). It is NOT a tool-row option: one behaviour for the whole
      # plugin belongs on the row that owns the plugin. With it on, a confined
      # run whose `--temp` private root (%TEMP%\dsh-<6 alphanumerics>) was
      # removed out of band recreates that directory and re-applies the seam's
      # write grant before the runner is spawned; with it off the command fails
      # exactly as upstream does. `tempWatchMs` is the interval of the
      # unattended safety net (default 10000 ms). Both are live: a saved value
      # applies without reloading a row.
      #   config:
      #     guardSandboxTemp: false
      #     tempWatchMs: 10000

    - id: win-mb-tool-git
      name: 'dsh-win-multi-bash/tool-git-bash'
      disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'
      # Optional per-machine executable pin (restate the whole partition when
      # uncommenting — a patch replaces the row's entire config). The value
      # below is a placeholder only — omit the pin entirely and let resolution
      # probe automatically (git.exe layout inference → well-known Program
      # Files on every fixed drive → PATH, with the WSL launcher and
      # WindowsApps aliases excluded):
      #   config:
      #     gitBash:
      #       bashPath: '<Git 安装目录>\usr\bin\bash.exe'
      #
      # Optional sandbox hardening: when the windows-acl probe fails (it cannot
      # confine MSYS bash), refuse to run unconfined unless the effective mode
      # is danger-full-access:
      #   config:
      #     gitBash:
      #       requireSandbox: true
      #
      # (The sandbox private-temp self-heal is NOT a row option: it is declared
      # once on the `win-mb-plugin` core row's own config, at the top of this
      # file, because it is one behaviour for the whole plugin.)

    - id: win-mb-tool-wsl
      name: 'dsh-win-multi-bash/tool-wsl-bash'
      # OPT-IN: only `git_bash` and the interactive terminal row are enabled by
      # default. A WSL deployment is a second toolchain a machine may not have,
      # and the row's first load probes it — so the row ships switched OFF and
      # the user enables it in the Plugins panel.
      disabled: true
      # Optional per-machine pins and hardening, same shape as the git row:
      #   wslBash:
      #     wslDistro: '<发行版名，如 Ubuntu-24.04>'
      #     wslPath: 'C:\Windows\System32\wsl.exe'
      #     requireSandbox: true

    - id: win-mb-tool-msys2
      name: 'dsh-win-multi-bash/tool-msys2-bash'
      # OPT-IN and Windows-only: the MSYS2 tool ships switched OFF, because the
      # MSYS2 installation is a second toolchain a user may not want mounted
      # alongside Git Bash. Enable this row in the Plugins panel to add it. Its
      # bash.exe is discovered under the installation roots the dialect declares
      # (on this machine the registry uninstall key HKCU ...\Uninstall\
      # {4b1a4d1b-9712-45ad-b2cb-b1b1eaccd0ee} answers D:\Local\msys64), or it can
      # be pinned per machine:
      #   msys2Bash:
      #     bashPath: '<MSYS2 安装目录>\usr\bin\bash.exe'
      disabled: true

    - id: win-mb-tool-ssh
      name: 'dsh-win-multi-bash/tool-ssh-shell'
      # OPT-IN and Windows-only: the row ships switched OFF until a deployment
      # declares at least one host in `sshShell.hosts`. It is the family's only
      # REMOTE dialect: its file effects are on the other host, so no local file
      # sandbox is applied and every FOREGROUND result carries
      # `sandbox: { mode, remote: true }` instead of a sandbox verdict; a promoted
      # (timed-out) call says so in its text, and a background acknowledgement
      # carries no `sandbox` field — the same two branches the base bundle's
      # `pwsh`/`bash` tools shape that way.
      #
      # Commands do NOT start a local ssh.exe: each call takes its own exec channel
      # on a connection POOLED per host (ssh2), sends the script on stdin and
      # reports the exit status with stdout and stderr separate. A call names its
      # host with `alias`; omitting it uses the one host marked `default: true`
      # (never "the first one"). The `terminal` row offers the same dialect for a
      # PERSISTENT session, and THAT form is the one that drives the OpenSSH client
      # with its own single-host pins (see the terminal row below).
      #
      # Declare the hosts this row may reach:
      #   sshShell:
      #     hosts:
      #       - alias: box
      #         host: '10.0.0.5'               # hostname or IP; no ssh_config aliases
      #         user: 'me'
      #         keyPath: '~/.ssh/id_ed25519'   # the KEY FILE is the only credential
      #         port: 22                       # optional, default 22
      #         default: true                  # what a call without `alias` uses
      #         acceptNewHostKeys: false       # learn an UNKNOWN key once; a CHANGED key still fails
      #         connectTimeoutMs: 15000        # handshake + authentication ceiling
      disabled: true

    # The interactive-session row: it registers the model-facing `terminal`
    # tool (open / send / read / signal / close / list). ONE row serves every
    # terminal-capable dialect — the `shell` argument enumerates the dialects
    # that declare the capability, derived from the registry — because a
    # session is a host-level resource: one registry, one session cap, one idle
    # reaper. Each dialect's interactive argv comes from its own executor
    # (`terminalArgv()`), so adding a dialect still changes nothing here.
    #
    # Sessions run UNCONFINED on purpose: the terminal primitive is a different
    # provider call than `spawn`, and the windows-acl runner cannot start MSYS
    # bash at all on this host, so there is no honest way to wrap one. Every
    # `open` reports that fact; set `terminal.allowUnconfined: false` to refuse
    # opening a session instead.
    - id: win-mb-tool-terminal
      name: 'dsh-win-multi-bash/tool-terminal'
      disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'
      # Session shape — every knob below is live-editable on the Plugins page:
      #   config:
      #     terminal:
      #       defaultShell: wsl_bash
      #       maxSessions: 8
      #       idleMs: 600000
      #       maxBufferBytes: 1048576
      #       allowUnconfined: true
      #
      # An SSH SESSION is the OpenSSH form: it does NOT read the command row's
      # `hosts` registry, it runs a local ssh.exe against ONE target, and its pins
      # live here. A real PTY is what lets ssh ask for a fingerprint, a password or
      # a passphrase.
      #   config:
      #     terminal:
      #       defaultShell: ssh_shell
      #       sshShell:
      #         sshPath: '<path to ssh.exe>'   # omit for the Windows OpenSSH client
      #         sshHost: '<host or ssh_config alias>'
      #         sshUser: '<user>'
      #         sshPort: 22
      #         acceptNewHostKeys: false       # learn an UNKNOWN key once; a CHANGED key still fails
      #         connectTimeoutMs: 15000        # connection-phase bound (ConnectTimeout)

readme.text: A Windows multi-bash plugin for DeepSeek Harness. **`git_bash`** (Git for Windows / MSYS) is on by default. **`wsl_bash`** (WSL), **`msys2_bash`** (MSYS2 UCRT64), **`ssh_shell`** (pooled SSH channels, key-only, many hosts) and **`ssh_scp`** (SFTP transfer on the same row) are opt-in. **`terminal`** keeps a real PTY session alive between calls.
Every dialect owns its own executor, and **no tool registers as `ctx.shell`** — that seat stays with the base bundle's pwsh, so pwsh behaves exactly as it does without this plugin.

| Tool | Backend | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `git_bash` | Git for Windows (MSYS) | **On by default**; owns a `GitBashExecutor` |
| `wsl_bash` | WSL Linux | **Opt-in**; owns a `WslBashExecutor`; its first load probes the distro |
| `msys2_bash` | MSYS2 UCRT64 | **Opt-in**; owns a `Msys2BashExecutor`; MSYS2's own `$MSYSTEM` and `pacman` |
| `ssh_shell` | Remote (SSH) | **Opt-in**; owns a `SshShellExecutor`; one pooled connection per host, one channel per call |
| `ssh_scp` | Remote (SSH) | **Opt-in with `ssh_shell`**; SFTP file/tree transfer on the same executor and pooled connection; foreground only |
| `terminal` | any of the above | Persistent PTY sessions: `open` / `send` / `read` / `signal` / `close` / `list` |
| `pwsh` | dsh's own | Untouched; served by the base bundle's `pwsh-sandbox` row |

Only `git_bash` and `terminal` ship on; the other three rows are opt-in. `git_bash` often runs unconfined — see [Sandbox behavior](https://github.com/Dinosaur-MC/dsh-win-multi-bash/blob/main/docs/sandbox.md).

- dsh `0.1.7-rc.2` through `0.2.x` — the window `package.json`'s `engines.dsh` declares. A newer dsh refuses this plugin.
- Windows, and a dsh deployment that provides the published `@deepseek-ai` base packages.
- Git Bash and/or WSL and/or MSYS2 only for the backends you enable; a missing backend never affects pwsh.
- For `ssh_shell` / `ssh_scp`: key-only access under `sshShell.hosts`, host keys in `known_hosts`.
- Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (the range this package declares), and `pnpm` for installation.

Install through `dsh plugin`, the pnpm forwarder: it applies this package's own `cordis.patch.yml` bundle layer, which inserts the rows.

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-win-multi-bash                    # npm package (recommended)
dsh plugin --profile web add github:@Dinosaur-MC/dsh-win-multi-bash # GitHub source
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-win-multi-bash                 # remove
```

Requires `pnpm`. The bundle layer is assembled at boot, so **restart `dsh web`** for a change to take effect. Do not also hand-write the same rows into the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: the loader rejects duplicate entry ids.

- **`git_bash`** is ready after install. It runs a fresh MSYS bash per call; `workdir` accepts native, MSYS (`/c/...`) and WSL automount (`/mnt/c/...`) forms.
- **`wsl_bash` / `msys2_bash`**: enable `win-mb-tool-wsl` / `win-mb-tool-msys2` on the Plugins page. Pin `wslBash.wslDistro` or `msys2Bash.bashPath` only when discovery is not enough.
- **`ssh_shell`**: enable `win-mb-tool-ssh` and add hosts under `sshShell.hosts` (`alias`, `host`, `user`, `keyPath`; `port` / `startupCommand` / `default` as needed). A call names an alias (or omits it when one host is `default`); no hosts refuses every call. Key-only auth, strict host keys — see the [migration notes](https://github.com/Dinosaur-MC/dsh-win-multi-bash/blob/main/docs/configuration.md). Hosts default to `approval: session`: one prompt per session through a dedicated card; `trusted` never asks.
- **`ssh_scp`**: the same row does transfers — `action: "upload" | "download"`, `localPath` (inside the workspace unless `danger-full-access`; checked lexically, symlinks are not resolved), `remotePath` (absolute POSIX; `/C:/...` on Windows OpenSSH), `recursive` for trees, `timeoutMs` (default 5 min). Foreground only; the result is `{ ok, by

- **Honest facts, not guesses.** A successful confined run says `denied: false`; a failed one matching the backend's denial dialect says `denied: true`; a failed one matching nothing says no `denied` at all. An unwrapped run says `unconfined: true`. A remote SSH run reports `sandbox: { mode, remote: true }`.
- **Platform-native calls.** Our shell tools use the platform's shell card; `ssh_scp` uses the generic row. See [Conversation rows](https://github.com/Dinosaur-MC/dsh-win-multi-bash/blob/main/docs/conversation-rows.md).
- **One connection per host, one channel per call.** `ssh_shell` reuses a pooled ssh2 client and gives every call its own exec channel — isolated, parallel-safe, cancellable. `ssh_scp` transfers share that pooled client, one SFTP session per transfer.
- **One declaration per dialect.** A dialect is one executor file plus one registry declaration; the tool modules, prompt membership, patch rows, config partition, package exports and client rows are derived from it. A declaration that does not hold together throws at load. See [Architecture](https://github.com/Dinosaur-MC/dsh-win-multi-bash/blob/main/docs/architecture.md).

The detailed documents are maintained in English; this README is the bilingual entry point and release summary.

```bash
npm ci                  # once: the pinned 0.2.1-rc.2 dev runtime
pnpm test               # boot a composition; run real commands; a verdict
pnpm run test:audit     # the full audit suite
DSH_AUDIT_SSH_HOST=ubuntu_tx node smoke/prepare.mjs audit   # optional live SSH

Both entries are development tools: the published tarball ships no `smoke/`. `pnpm test` fails on a missing tool, a wrong description, a lost `ctx.shell` seat or a failed command; the audit announces and counts its skips.

```
dsh-win-multi-bash/
├── package.json            # dsh.bundle + dsh.client + engines.dsh; exports for every tool subpath
├── cordis.patch.yml        # the composition wiring (documented inline)
├── lib/                    # plain ESM implementation (no build step)

`docs/` and `smoke/` are repository-only; `npm pack` ships only the files listed in `package.json`.
